title: IzhiRISC-V - a RISC-V-based Processor with Custom ISA Extension for Spiking Neuron Networks Processing with Izhikevich Neurons
problem: General-purpose RISC-V processors are inefficient for Spiking Neural Network (SNN) processing due to repeated use of basic instructions for neuron state updates; efficiency gains from sparsity are undermined.
motivation: Spiking neural networks promise high energy efficiency from sparse spike events, but this advantage is lost on general-purpose hardware without specialized instruction support.
method: This processor extends RISC-V with custom neuromorphic instructions (brain-mimicking operations designed for neural computation) that compute Izhikevich neuron state updates directly. Instead of requiring many basic arithmetic steps per neuron update, each custom instruction handles the entire Izhikevich calculation in a single operation. These instructions are implemented by expanding the ALU (the arithmetic logic unit) to natively execute these specialized operations.
key_novelty: This is the first RISC-V processor to include custom neuromorphic instructions designed specifically for Izhikevich neuron computations.
contributions: Custom ISA extension for spiking neuron updates
limitations: Abstract-only; lacks performance numbers, energy measurements, or comparison to other SNN accelerators
